doc.title: Nancy Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Australia trip, marriage and living in California
summary: After the first album she went to Australia on John Levy's plan, returned a sensation, married in California in 1960, and explains why she prefers California to New York.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: How long have you been on the west coast?

Since the first, let’s see I did the first album in December. The first album came out in April. And I left then and went to Australia and waited for it to start flowing. John and I did that. It was so cute I loved it. I spent months in Australia waiting. And I was not available when the first record started hitting the air.
I was out of the country working. I had months booked there, and came back, and was a sensation.
This was something that was thought of at the time?
Yeah. When this starts to happen you won’t be here. They’ll have to ask for you.

That’s John Levy. I love him so, I just love him. So that worked out very well. And I came back from Australia in December of ‘60 and was married in California. I came here and moved to California. I really prefer it. I’m from a rural atmosphere. I’m from basically outside of the city limits. I’m not an inner city person. I can’t deal — I came to New York and the first year it was oh my God these tall buildings and where is the sun, where is the grass, I want to see a tree that is not in Central Park. So I have, it was quite an adjustment for me from the midwest coming to the East Coast. I basically have loved California. And I love the south. I could live in Atlanta. I could live in North Carolina. I like that. But I think I’m forever in California. I’m a desert rat although I’m basically Pisces and I love the water, I do live in the desert. And it’s probably because it’s more economical. I lived at the beach for years, and then I moved my family to the desert. My husband and I used to have two places at the desert, but the girls and I are back at the beach. So we just have a, I’ll tell you I’ve really been blessed. I’m able to be ten minutes from The Strand, which is one of the few places that has a room that’s really amenable for work and good for working. I can take the trio in and we can have a good time in there. I still play Carnegie Hall. I’ll be back in New York at the Blue Note actually in the new year again here at the Blue Note, and stay for the week after and do six nights. But I do enjoy New York to play. There’s an excitement here you can’t find anyplace else. So I do love Carnegie Hall. I have a good time here. Don’t want to live here. I want to come here and party, sing, have a good time.
